column6: the QR bit is read into a local that nothing reads back — it appears twice in the file, once of them in the licence header — so both readings assign a value nobody observes. Not checking it is conformant besides: RFC 5452 6.1 enumerates what a resolver MUST match a response against, and the six are the addresses, the port, the ID, the name, the class and the type. QR is not among them

the left-most label of a parsed host name cannot be empty — DomainName refuses an empty label before Matches is ever reached — so this guard has nothing to guard against. The comment above it says as much: "the check costs nothing and this is the wrong place to find out"
